FUSION ADD-IN DOCUMENTATION

Export Selected to DXF (v1.5.3)
One DXF per selected sketch, curve set, face, body or flat pattern — from a dark panel inside Autodesk Fusion

Swami Autodesk Fusion add-in Version 1.5.3 · released Nov 1, 2026
⬇ Download ExportSelectedToDXF.zip
How to install

Mac and Windows. Nothing to approve, because no installer script runs.

  1. Unzip ExportSelectedToDXF.zip and put the ExportSelectedToDXF folder somewhere it can stay, for example in Documents. Fusion runs the add-in from that folder.
  2. In Fusion, open Scripts and Add-Ins: press Shift+S, or click the UTILITIES tab, open the ADD-INS drop-down and choose Scripts and Add-Ins.
  3. Click the + next to My Add-Ins and choose the ExportSelectedToDXF folder.
  4. Turn on Run and Run on Startup for ExportSelectedToDXF.
  5. The button is on the SOLID tab under CREATE, and under UTILITIES ▸ ADD-INS.

Copies the add-in into Fusion's own AddIns folder. macOS blocks it the first time.

  1. Unzip ExportSelectedToDXF.zip, open the ExportSelectedToDXF folder and double-click install-macos.command.
  2. macOS says it could not verify the file. Click Done (not Move to Trash).
  3. Open System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security, and next to "install-macos.command was blocked" click Open Anyway. Confirm with Open Anyway again and your Mac password or Touch ID.
  4. A Terminal window copies the add-in and says Done. Press any key to close it.
  5. In Fusion, open Scripts and Add-Ins: press Shift+S, or click the UTILITIES tab, open the ADD-INS drop-down and choose Scripts and Add-Ins. Select ExportSelectedToDXF under Add-Ins and turn on Run and Run on Startup.
  6. macOS asks again for every newly downloaded zip. Updates from the panel's install update button never ask.

Copies the add-in into Fusion's own AddIns folder.

  1. Right-click ExportSelectedToDXF.zip and choose Extract All (the installer can't run from inside the zip).
  2. Open the extracted ExportSelectedToDXF folder and double-click install-windows.cmd.
  3. If Windows shows Windows protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway. If it shows an Open File - Security Warning, click Run.
  4. A window copies the add-in and says Done. Press any key to close it.
  5. In Fusion, open Scripts and Add-Ins: press Shift+S, or click the UTILITIES tab, open the ADD-INS drop-down and choose Scripts and Add-Ins. Select ExportSelectedToDXF under Add-Ins and turn on Run and Run on Startup.

01Dashboard SummaryOverview▶

Export Selected to DXF is a free Autodesk Fusion add-in that exports whatever you have selected (whole sketches, some curves of a sketch, planar faces, solid bodies and sheet-metal flat patterns) as one DXF file per item, from a dark panel that stays open while you work. This page documents the current version, which is shown in the title; What's New lists every release. Terms with a dotted underline jump to the Glossary.

Start hereNew to the add-in? Go to Install & Update, then The Panel. Already using it? What's New shows what changed in each version.

04The PanelFeature▶

Click the add-in's button, in SOLID ▸ CREATE or UTILITIES ▸ ADD-INS, to open the panel; click it again to hide it. The panel opens floating in the top-right corner of Fusion's canvas and stays open while you work. Its height follows the sections you open and close, but never runs past the bottom of the canvas. Every time it opens, each section starts in its default state shown below.

PartWhat it doesStarts
reset to defaultsTop-right corner. Asks first, then restores every option to its factory default.Always shown
Update bannerGreen banner shown when a newer version is out, with install update, download and what's new.Only when an update exists
ExportLive selection summary (for example "4 selected → 4 files"), the EXPORT SELECTED button, and the folder and units the files will use. The header still shows the selection count when collapsed.Open
OutputFolder (with browse and open buttons), units, file naming, overwrite, open the folder afterward.Closed
Sketches & facesWhether construction geometry, sketch points and projected geometry go into the file.Closed
Flat patternsBend center lines, bend extent lines, spline-to-polyline conversion and its tolerance.Closed
Last exportEach file written with its curve count and size, plus anything skipped and why. Opens by itself when something didn't export.Closed
LogRunning history of exports, update checks and errors, with all/problems filter, copy, open log file and clear at the top.Closed
UpdatesWhether to check for a newer version when the panel opens, plus a check now button.Closed
AboutThe installed version, then links: documentation opens this page, release notes opens the notes for your version, download latest downloads the newest zip, and all versions opens the release list on GitHub. Hover over each for a tooltip. Also the credit.Closed
ErrorsAnything unexpected from Fusion appears in a red strip at the top of the panel (click it to dismiss) and is also written to the Log.
05What You Can SelectFeature▶

Select any mix of these in the canvas or the browser. Each item becomes its own file; anything that can't be exported is listed in Last export and the Log with the reason.

You selectHow it's exportedFile name (Component - Item)
A sketch, or every curve of oneThe whole sketch, exported directlyFRAME - frame-center.dxf
Some curves of a sketchThe chosen curves are copied into a temporary sketch at their original position, exported, and the temporary sketch is deletedComponent - sketch name (selected).dxf
A planar faceA temporary sketch is made on the face, its outline exported, and the sketch deletedComponent - body face 1.dxf
A solid bodyIts largest flat face, exported like a planar faceComponent - body.dxf
A sheet-metal body or componentIts flat pattern. If the part has no flat pattern yet, one is created first and left in the partComponent - Flat Pattern.dxf
A flat patternExported directly with your bend-line settingsComponent - Flat Pattern.dxf
Anything elseSkipped, with the reason shown—
No overwrites by defaultIf a file with the same name exists, the new one gets -2, -3 and so on. Turn on Overwrite existing files in Output to replace instead.

07UnitsFusion API▶

Units are a real export setting, not a conversion afterward. Sketch and flat-pattern exports both pass the chosen unit to Fusion, which writes the matching unit header into the file. Design units leaves the setting alone, so the file uses whatever the design is set to.

Units optionResultUnit header in file
MillimetersExported correctly$INSUNITS = 4 (millimeters)
InchesExported correctly, sketches and flat patterns$INSUNITS = 1 (inches)
Preview featureAutodesk marks the sketch export call with the units setting as a preview feature. If a future Fusion removes it, the add-in falls back to the older save method, which still exports but uses design units and includes all geometry.
08Things to KnowNotes▶
  • ConstructionConstruction geometry is off by default, which suits laser and CNC work. Turn it on in Sketches & faces if you need it.
  • Flat patternsWhen a sheet-metal part has no flat pattern, the add-in creates one (its largest flat face stays put) and leaves it in the part, exactly as Fusion's own Create Flat Pattern would. It appears in the browser under the part.
  • SplinesSplines-to-polylines works for flat patterns only; Fusion's sketch export has no such option.
  • Curved facesOnly planar faces can be laid flat; a curved face is skipped with the reason "not planar".
  • Partial sketchesExporting only some curves of a sketch adds "(selected)" to the file name so it can't be mistaken for the whole sketch.
  • TimelineTemporary sketches for faces and partial selections are deleted right after each export, so the timeline is left as it was.

12How the Export WorksFusion API▶

Each export path is a short sequence of Fusion API calls. Nothing is exported by simulating clicks, so results are the same whatever is on screen.

PathAPI callsWhat it controls
SketchExportManager.createDXFSketchExportOptionsUnits, construction geometry, sketch points, projected geometry
Sketch fallbackSketch.saveAsDXFNothing; design units and all geometry
Partial sketchSketches.add, Sketch.copy (identity transform), then the sketch export, then deleteMeSame as a sketch
Face or solid bodySketches.add on the face (Fusion projects its edges), then the sketch export, then deleteMeSame as a sketch
Flat patternComponent.createFlatPattern when none exists, then ExportManager.createDXFFlatPatternExportOptionsUnits, bend center lines, bend extent lines, spline-to-polyline conversion
  • SelectionThe add-in listens for Fusion's selection-changed event, so the Export section's count follows your clicks while the panel is visible.
  • Update checkEvery time the panel opens (at most once every two minutes), a background thread reads a fresh copy of version.json from GitHub and hands the result back to Fusion's main thread through a custom event.
  • Install updateDownloads the latest zip, checks it is a newer ExportSelectedToDXF package with safe file paths, backs up the current files, replaces them, and restores the backup if anything fails.
  • Panel heightThe page measures how much content is hidden or spare and asks Fusion to resize the panel by that amount, then re-measures until it fits. It never grows past the bottom of the canvas.
  • Panel positionWhen the panel opens it is placed in the top-right corner of Fusion's canvas, using the canvas position Fusion reports for the active viewport.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
PanelFusion UIThe add-in's dockable window (a Fusion palette) that stays open while you work, unlike a command dialog.
Add-inFusion UIA Python program that loads into Fusion, can run at startup, and adds its own buttons and panels.
TimelineFusion UIThe history bar at the bottom of a Fusion design that records every feature and sketch in order.
DXFExportDrawing Exchange Format, the 2D file format most laser, plasma and CNC software reads.
Unit headerExportThe $INSUNITS entry in a DXF file that tells other software which unit the coordinates are in.
Design unitsExportThe default length unit set in a design's Document Settings.
Temporary sketchExportA sketch the add-in creates only to hold geometry for one export, then deletes.
CNCExportComputer numerical control: machines such as routers and mills that cut from toolpaths.
Sketch curveGeometryA line, arc, circle or spline inside a sketch.
Planar faceGeometryA flat face of a solid body. Only planar faces can be laid flat in a DXF.
Construction geometryGeometryReference curves in a sketch, shown dashed, used for layout but not meant to be cut.
Projected geometryGeometryCurves copied into a sketch from edges, faces or other sketches.
Sketch pointsGeometryStandalone points in a sketch, such as hole centers.
SplineGeometryA smooth freeform curve. Some CAM and laser software handles splines poorly.
PolylineGeometryA chain of short straight segments that approximates a curve within a set tolerance.
Flat patternSheet MetalThe unfolded 2D layout of a sheet-metal part, with its bends shown as lines.
Sheet metalSheet MetalFusion's tools for modeling bent parts from flat stock of a set thickness.
Bend linesSheet MetalLines on a flat pattern showing where to bend: center lines mark the middle of each bend, extent lines where it starts and ends.
Fusion APIAPIAutodesk's programming interface that add-ins and scripts use to control Fusion.
Preview featureAPIAn API call Autodesk has released early and may change or remove later.
Custom eventAPIFusion's way for a background thread to hand a result back to the main thread safely.
Install updateUpdatesThe button in the panel's green banner that downloads and installs the newest version in place.
version.jsonUpdatesA small file on GitHub naming the latest version; the add-in reads it to know when an update exists.
ReleaseUpdatesA published version on GitHub, with its zip attached and release notes.
BackupUpdatesA copy of the previous version that install update saves before replacing files.
LogFilesThe running history of exports, update checks and errors, shown in the panel and saved to log.txt.
settings.jsonFilesThe per-user file that remembers your options, kept outside the add-in folder.
InstallerFilesAn optional double-click script that copies the add-in into Fusion's AddIns folder.
ManifestFilesThe small file Fusion reads to list an add-in: its name, version and supported systems.
